text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Canada supports the restructuring of Romania's oil sector, the paper said.
- Workers at the Mefin precision tooling plant in Sinaia protested against plans by the administration to privatise and restructure the plant.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Romania is unable to start the privatisation process of its commercial banks this year, the paper said.
- Romtelecom RA telephone operator hopes to get a $200 million credit from EBRD to upgrade its infrastructure.
- The Agriculture Ministry asked the government to supplement with 250 billion lei the fund for grain purchases this year.
- The SNCFR railway authority sold 25,000 tonnes of scrap iron.
- Trade unions at Renel RA electricity authority oppose plans by the administration to restructure the company.
General:
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- German Chancellor Helmut Kohl will support Romania's bid for an early NATO admission, the paper said.
- The ruling centrist coalition is challanged by disputes between its main members, the National Peasants Party and Democractic Party, the paper says.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Prosecutors investigate local businessman George Paunescu over alleged attempts to undermine the national economy, the paper said.
- President Emil Constantinescu met German Chancellor Helmut Kohl in Bonn in a bid to get Germany's support for Romania to get into NATO. enlargement.
ADEVARUL
- New legislation approved by the government might put an end to illegal adoptions in Romania, the paper says.
- The paper quotes Bucharest police chief Colonel Virgil Ardeleanu as saying he would support initiatives to legalise prostitution in the country.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
